summary: How many triangles a runtime mesh should cost, decided from what the asset is and how big it is. A profile's maximum_triangles is a ceiling for gates, never a target. A closed mesh has about two triangles per vertex, so an ordinary prop at 10,000 triangles is about 5,000 vertices.

size_classes.description: fits in a hand: coins, shards, gauges
a stool, a lantern, a pot
a chest, a brazier, a person-sized thing
a cart, a doorway, a big machine
a colossal statue, a bridge span

roles.description: Anything that will be rigged and animated. Characters take the rig route, whose skeleton profile carries its own budget.
A set piece the player stops and looks at: thrones, statues, shrines, the centrepiece of a room.
Plants, vines and roots: many thin parts, so a little more than a prop of the same size.
Kit pieces placed many times along walls, floors and stairs. They are paid for every time they repeat, so they cost by length.
roles.elongation_comment: Kit pieces are long and thin: rails, trim, pipes, beams. A 'chain winch' or a pillar's square base is not, whatever its name says, and is budgeted as a prop.

roles.description: Everything else you can walk up to, pick up or bump into: chests, braziers, urns, tools, furniture.

notes_rule: Notes mention neighbours and parts ('stands on a plinth', a door's 'independent leaves'), so they promote only through a role's notes_keywords, never its broader name keywords, and only to a role with notes_min_size when the asset is at least that big.
notes_comment: A name decides first. Notes may only raise a role (a 'toppled giant statue head' is a hero piece); they never make something cheaper, because notes mention neighbouring things ('stands on a plinth') far more often than names do.

deviation.comment: The reduction must stay this close to the reviewed surface, scaled to the object so a colossus is not held to a coin's tolerance.

ladder.comment: When the surface gates refuse a budget, try the next rung rather than shipping damage. Stop once a rung would keep most of the source: then the source is the answer.
